Timeline::seconds_between¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

std::int64_t Timeline::seconds_between(const Timeline& other) const

Count Complete Elapsed Seconds¶

seconds_between() returns the signed count of complete one-billion-nanosecond units from the scalar receiver to scalar other. Fractional seconds are truncated toward zero. The operation uses absolute epoch instants, not local calendar fields, and therefore permits different timezone labels.

The 64-bit return type is part of the contract. Timeline’s supported range can span far more than the roughly 68 years representable by signed 32-bit seconds. Internally, subtraction is widened before division so distant valid endpoints cannot overflow merely because their raw nanosecond ticks have opposite signs.

Example: Fractional Seconds Do Not Round¶

const auto start = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z");
const auto end = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-02T02:03:04.500000000Z");

std::cout << start.seconds_between(end) << '\n'
          << end.seconds_between(start) << '\n';

Output¶

93784
-93784

The trailing half-second is discarded in both directions. The reverse result is not -93785 because division truncates toward zero rather than flooring.

Example: The Result Exceeds 32-Bit Range Safely¶

const auto early = pluss::timeline::make("1700-01-01T00:00:00Z");
const auto late = pluss::timeline::make("2200-01-01T00:00:00Z");

std::cout << early.seconds_between(late) << '\n'
          << late.seconds_between(early) << '\n';

Output¶

15778454400
-15778454400

This interval also makes the direct nanosecond subtraction exceed signed 64-bit range. Widening before subtraction preserves the correct quotient.

Example: Timezone Conversion Preserves The Instant¶

const auto utc = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z");
const auto local = utc.tz_convert("America/Edmonton");

std::cout << utc.seconds_between(local) << '\n';

Output¶

0

Example: NaT And Arrays Are Not Scalar Distances¶

const auto start = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z");

for (const auto& other : {
         pluss::timeline::make(""),
         pluss::timeline::make({"2024-01-01", "2024-01-02"}),
     }) {
  try {
    (void)start.seconds_between(other);
  } catch (const pluss::Error&) {
    std::cout << "rejected\n";
  }
}

Output¶

rejected
rejected

The method performs constant work, allocates nothing, and never mutates either operand. Use span() when the inputs are arrays or a subsecond unit such as milliseconds, microseconds, or nanoseconds is required.
